# ui::HighContrastPalette

Header: `winui/ui/themes/ThemeSource.hpp`.

The colors of the system's contrast theme, used as they are. The defaults are black on white, so a default-constructed [OsThemeSnapshot](os-theme-snapshot.md) is usable without setting every field.

These are the eight colors a user picks in a contrast theme, plus a border color.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::OsThemeSnapshot os;
os.high_contrast = true;
os.hc            = ui::HighContrastPalette::windows10_high_contrast_black();

// A contrast theme is on: the window draws with the palette the user picked.
window.pin_theme(ui::resolve_theme(ui::ThemeRequest{}, os));
```

## aquatic

```cpp
static HighContrastPalette aquatic()
```

Aquatic, the contrast theme Windows 11 turns on when Left Alt+Left Shift+Print Screen is pressed and no contrast theme was chosen before. The border color is not one a user picks, so it takes [`control_text`](#control_text), the color contrast themes draw control borders in.

Fluent 2 uses these colors when an app forces `ThemeMode::HighContrast` while the system has no contrast theme on.

## windows10_high_contrast_black

```cpp
static HighContrastPalette windows10_high_contrast_black()
```

High Contrast Black as Windows 8 through 10 ship it, designed for a 14:1 contrast ratio. The border takes [`control_text`](#control_text), as in [`aquatic()`](#aquatic). Metro, MDL2 and Fluent use it when high contrast is forced.
